evals.expected_output: For the first method, the skill should identify the Command-Query Separation (CQS) violation — the method both mutates state (_counter) and returns a value. It should recommend splitting into increment_counter() (command, mutates state, returns nothing) and current_id() (query, pure, no side effects). For the second method, the skill should apply Consolidate Conditional Expression — combine all three conditions into a single expression, ideally extracted into a clearly named helper or collapsed into a one-liner using 'or'.
assertions: Identifies the CQS (Command-Query Separation) violation in get_next_available_id — it both mutates state and returns a value
Proposes splitting into a command (increment_counter or similar, returns nothing) and a query (current_id or similar, pure read)
Applies Consolidate Conditional Expression to is_eligible_for_discount — combines the three separate if-return-True blocks into a single expression
Explains the CQS principle: a method should either answer a question or perform an action, never both
